The two manuals disagree on the CAN RJ45 GND pin. Rack manual table 3.6.3-2: pin 2 = GND, pins 1,3,6,7,8 = NC. Wall manual table 6: pins 1,2,3,6,8 grouped, pin 7 = GND. Both agree pin 4 = CAN-H and pin 5 = CAN-L. Do not solder a cable from one document alone.

Parallel-count contradiction inside one manual: table 2.4 says 'hasta 63 unidades en paralelo', §3.6.4 says 'permite operar hasta 40 dispositivos en paralelo'. The 200E datasheet says 63. The DIP table enumerates 0–63.

DIP-range contradiction inside one manual: the component table (item 4) says 'Configuración de dirección (rango 2 a 15)', while table 3.6.3-3 that it points at enumerates addresses 0 through 63 across six switches. The wall manual repeats the same '2~15' claim next to its own 0–63 table.
unmappedReports: Fault / alarm / protection code. The manuals carry a Fault Alarm Handling Table naming ~15 distinct alarms (charging high-temperature, MOSFET high-temperature, single-cell overvoltage, ambient low-temperature, …) and there is no MetricKind for a fault or alarm code at all. This is the same gap can-bms.md already flagged for EPEver and Victron; three vendors now., Charge-current limit and discharge-current limit as REPORTED values. CommandKind::SetChargeCurrentLimit exists to write one; no MetricKind exists to read back what the pack is asking for, which is the single most important number a BMS sends an inverter., Pack index within a parallel cluster. The DIP sets an address 0–63 and readings are polled per pack; nothing in the contract expresses which of N packs a value came from., MOSFET temperature. 'MOSFET High-Temperature Alarm' is a named fault; MetricKind has battery-temperature and temperature (ambient), neither of which is a FET junction., Number of packs online / cluster size. Without it a summed bank reading cannot be sanity-checked.
